newsitem.title: UK: CWS paid by Hambros, Travers in settlement.
newsitem.headline: CWS paid by Hambros, Travers in settlement.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) received a "substantial" financial settlement when it dropped legal action against investment bank Hambros and law firm Travers Smith Braithwaite on Monday, sources close to the company said.

CWS received unreserved apologies from both Hambros and Travers after it threatened them with legal action stemming from their role as advisers to Andrew Regan and his firm Galileo in its abortive attempt to take over the CWS.

The sources said the two financial settlements, which all parties have agreed not to discuss publicly, involved "a substantial sum". CWS is continuing both civil and criminal proceedings against Regan and others.

Last week, CWS executive Alan Prescott, who has led the internal enquiry into the affair, said the defence of the takeover bid had cost it millions of pounds. He predicted, however, that CWS would not be left "out of pocket".

CWS would only say that it had reached a "satisfactory" settlement with both parties who had advised on Galileo's 1.2 billion pounds ($1.9 billion) plan to turn mutually-owned CWS into a limited company and break it up.

Throughout the bid saga, CWS chief Graham Melmoth had repeatedly questioned Hambros and Travers Smith about their roles and the use of confidential information leaked to Regan by former CWS executive Allan Green who was sacked over the weekend.
